microStakeSkeleton: Late at night, on the road that leads from the minshuku toward the edge of town. A stranger is leaning against a wooden fence, looking up at the sky. They greet you softly, as if they had been expecting someone — but maybe not you specifically. They ask where you're headed, or whether you've ever noticed something particular about this stretch of road. Their register is hard to place: not formal, not casual — just a little out of time.
allowedNudges: If the player goes quiet, the stranger doesn't push — they look back at the sky and say something softer, almost to themselves, that the player can pick up if they want.
The stranger may slip in a half-question that doesn't quite need an answer, lowering pressure.
exitBeat: The stranger gives a small wave, says you should probably head back before the wind picks up, and turns toward the dark.
